name: Oxytocin nasal spray

card.summary: A bonding-hormone spray sold online; real social-neuroscience research behind the hormone, but no study backs it as a looks or ascension tool.
card.aka: Intranasal oxytocin, OT spray, "love hormone" spray
card.note: Oxytocin is prescription-only in the US and UK; online peptide-spray kits are unregulated products.

quick.overview:
Oxytocin is a nine-amino-acid hormone made in the hypothalamus that is involved in childbirth, milk ejection and social bonding. Hospitals use injected or infused oxytocin to induce labor and control bleeding after delivery. Intranasal versions have been studied in laboratories for effects on trust, social perception and anxiety.

In looksmaxxing and peptide communities it is discussed as a spray for sociability, bonding or mood, and in separate threads as a hormone to be "reset" after attachment to a person. No published trial has tested it for improving facial appearance or physical attractiveness.
quick.mechanism: Oxytocin binds the oxytocin receptor, a G-protein-coupled receptor found in the uterus, mammary glands and several brain regions. Given into the nose, it is thought to reach brain circuits involved in social cognition, and lab studies report reduced amygdala responses to fearful faces and altered behaviour in trust games. Results vary by person and context.
quick.risks: Systemic oxytocin in obstetrics is a high-alert medication with risks such as uterine hyperstimulation and water intoxication at excessive doses. Short-term research doses by nose have not produced serious adverse events in published studies, but long-term data are limited. Oxytocin is a prescription drug in the US and UK, and gray-market spray kits sold online are not regulated for purity or concentration.

lead: Oxytocin is a peptide hormone of nine amino acids made mainly in the hypothalamus and released from the posterior pituitary. It acts on the uterus during labor, on the breast during lactation, and on brain circuits involved in social behaviour [1][9]. A synthetic form is a standard obstetric drug given by infusion or injection [16].

Oxytocin nasal spray refers to preparations delivered into the nose so that the peptide can act on the brain. In research it has been used in short-term experiments on trust, social cognition, fear processing and conditions such as autism and frontotemporal dementia [3][5][6]. Online vendors and peptide communities also sell or discuss spray kits aimed at mood, sociability and bonding.

Published findings on intranasal oxytocin in humans are mixed, and reviewers have emphasised that its effects depend on the person and the situation [4]. No published human trial has examined intranasal oxytocin for facial appearance, bone structure or attractiveness, which are the typical goals of looksmaxxing.

paras: Oxytocin is a cyclic nonapeptide encoded by the OXT gene and made in magnocellular neurons of the hypothalamus. It is released into the blood from the posterior pituitary and also acts as a neurotransmitter within the brain [1][2]. Its receptor is a G-protein-coupled receptor present in uterine muscle, the mammary gland and brain regions linked to social behaviour [1].

Intranasal oxytocin is used in research because the hormone given by the bloodstream has a very short half-life and poor entry to the brain. Wikipedia reports that intravenous oxytocin has a half-life of around three minutes, while intranasal dosing has been associated with a central duration of a few hours [16]. How much of an intranasal dose reaches the brain directly, versus acting through the periphery, remains debated in the literature.

In obstetrics, oxytocin is given by intravenous infusion or intramuscular injection to induce or strengthen labor and to reduce bleeding after delivery, and it is on the WHO List of Essential Medicines [16]. It was added to the Institute for Safe Medication Practices high-alert list in 2012 because of the harm that can follow dosing errors [16].
Intranasal oxytocin is not approved in the US for social anxiety, autism or other behavioural conditions, although these have been research targets [2].
No studies found on intranasal oxytocin for appearance, facial structure or attractiveness. Studies of intranasal oxytocin for other purposes include the following.

A widely cited 2005 Nature study reported that participants who received intranasal oxytocin showed more trust in a monetary game with another person than those given placebo [3]. Later reviews concluded that social effects of oxytocin in humans depend on context and on individual differences, and that findings were not uniform [4]. A neuroimaging study reported that intranasal oxytocin reduced amygdala activation to fearful faces and weakened its coupling with brainstem regions [5]. A broader review described oxytocin and vasopressin as social neuropeptides of interest for translational medicine [6].

Registered trials include a phase 2 study of intranasal oxytocin in hypothalamic obesity (18 participants, completed) [7], a phase 2 trial in frontotemporal dementia (112 participants, status unknown) [8], and a phase 2 study of peripheral oxytocin and touch in healthy adults (20 participants, completed) [17]. Wikipedia notes a 2013 meta-analysis in which only autism spectrum disorder showed a significant pooled effect, and a 2022 study that found an effect in children aged 3 to 5 but not 5 to 12 [16]. Grokipedia states that NIH-funded trials found no significant improvement in social functioning in autism and that, in social anxiety, intranasal oxytocin did not enhance the outcome of exposure therapy [10].

Wikipedia reports that short-term intranasal doses of 18 to 40 IU in research have not been associated with recorded serious adverse effects [16]. By contrast, systemic oxytocin in obstetrics can cause uterine hyperstimulation, and prolonged or excessive dosing is linked to water intoxication, seizures and uterine rupture [16].

Long-term safety of repeated self-directed intranasal use has not been studied in controlled trials. Compounded or gray-market products have no consistent quality oversight, and counterfeit oxytocin products have been reported in some countries [16].

Henry Dale described the uterus-contracting action of pituitary extract in 1906, and Ott and Scott reported milk-ejection effects in 1910 [16][10]. Vincent du Vigneaud determined the structure of oxytocin and synthesised it in 1953, the first peptide hormone made synthetically, and received the 1955 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for the work [16].
Research on its social effects expanded in the 2000s, notably after the 2005 trust experiment [3] and work on its role in social stress buffering [11].

Online vendors have marketed oxytocin and other peptides as nasal sprays for sociability and bonding. A looksmax.org thread discusses a UK peptide spray kit that includes a dilution check for N-acetyl semax alongside oxytocin [12]. Other threads discuss testing oxytocin together with growth hormone and parathyroid hormone analogs [13] and experimenting with oxytocin spray in connection with the "ndpill", a community term for a belief about nondating outcomes [14].

Separately, some looksmaxxing users talk about oxytocin as a feeling to be reduced after romantic attachment. One thread asks how to "nuke" oxytocin after meeting a woman; a reply suggests the hormone is useful for bone growth and another proposes seeking rejection to end the feeling [15]. These are individual forum opinions, not research findings.

lore.intro: Oxytocin spray appears in looksmaxxing forums mostly in peptide-kit threads and in discussions of bonding and attachment rather than as a facial-improvement tool [12][13].

claims.claim: Oxytocin spray can fix social anxiety or the "ndpill" mindset.
claims.believers: A user thread describes experimenting with intranasal oxytocin to change social outcomes and attitudes [14].
claims.experts: Trials of intranasal oxytocin in social anxiety and autism have had mixed results, and it is not approved for these uses [4][10].

claims.claim: Oxytocin from sex or relationships can be "nuked" or avoided by following specific routines.
claims.believers: Forum posters describe unwanted attachment feelings and trade suggestions for ending them, including being rejected [15].
claims.experts: Research describes oxytocin as one of several neuromodulators in bonding, with effects that depend on context and individual, and no controlled study tests ways to deliberately remove such feelings [4][11].

claims.claim: Oxytocin supports bone growth, so it is relevant to facial structure.
claims.believers: One forum reply says oxytocin is good for bone growth and recommends keeping it [15].
claims.experts: Grokipedia reports that oxytocin acts on osteoblasts and bone metabolism in lab and physiological work [10]. No published study examines intranasal oxytocin for facial bone structure in humans.

claims.claim: Peptide spray kits combining oxytocin with other compounds are a convenient way to use these peptides.
claims.believers: Threads discuss kits and dilution checks for sprays containing oxytocin and semax [12].
claims.experts: Regulators treat oxytocin as a prescription drug, and no standards govern concentration or purity in gray-market kits [16].
